newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Oil barges barely hit by Antwerp port strike.
newsitem.headline: Oil barges barely hit by Antwerp port strike.

text.p: Oil barge operators in the Rotterdam-Antwerp area said on Friday they faced few hardships from this week's strike in Antwerp.
"There have been a few minor problems (getting) to inner Belgium, but that's about it. As for the Rotterdam-Antwerp route, there have been no problems at all," said one Rotterdam operator.

The operators said that the lock closures resulting from the strike meant some journeys, such as from Antwerp to Ghent, were extended by about two or three hours, due to rerouting away from inland canals.

Cargoes faced slightly greater problems. Shippers said a few had been slightly delayed. The larger size of such vessels means they can only use the largest locks where, the operators said, the strike action was focused.
"I have had a sea-going vessel delayed by about two days, but my barges are fine," said one shipper in Antwerp.
On Thursday, an Antwerp port authority spokesman said the then three-day-old strike was rapidly losing its impact as most locks giving entry to the port had reopened.
Port authority workers have been on strike in protest over a planned change in their status from public sector to private sector employees.
